condition: Colorectal cancer screening — family history with Lynch-syndrome features
permutationLabel: Age 41, sister CRC at 48, mother endometrial cancer at 55
summary: 41-year-old woman, sister diagnosed with colorectal cancer at 48 (tumour MMR status unknown), mother endometrial cancer at 55. Increased-risk screening (colonoscopy from 40, 5-yearly) and suspicion of Lynch syndrome (tumour MMR testing / genetics referral).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Worried about bowel cancer — sister recently diagnosed
inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 41-year-old woman. Her younger sister was diagnosed with colon cancer at 48 last year (right colon, operated abroad; not known whether the tumour was tested for mismatch repair). Mother had womb (endometrial) cancer at 55. No bowel symptoms. Never had a colonoscopy.
comorbidities: Family history: sister colorectal cancer at 48
Family history: mother endometrial cancer at 55

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Family history of colorectal cancer (FDR < 50) with possible Lynch syndrome — asymptomatic
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic. Sister colorectal cancer at 48, mother endometrial cancer at 55: increased-risk family history with Lynch features. Colonoscopy now (from 40, 5-yearly); request sister's tumour MMR/MSI result; clinical genetics referral.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage: the family-history comorbidity text contains 'cancer', which scanRedFlags reads as 'Possible malignancy' (priority), and 'cancer' also counts as a higher-risk comorbidity → same_day_call for an asymptomatic screening consultation.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Treat topic words ('cancer screening', a relative's cancer) as context rather than a current malignancy red flag, and treat 'no change in bowel habit' as negated (the matcher currently handles 'no change' as a pseudo-negation).

mustInclude.note: One FDR with CRC < 60: colonoscopy from 40 (or 10 years before the youngest case), 5-yearly. Web harness limit: the web runner passes familyHistory: [] to computeClinicalPrompts (the vignette schema has no family-history field). Calling computeClinicalPrompts directly with the dashboard's 'Colorectal cancer' family-history chip at 41 produces 'Arrange colonoscopy — FHx CRC, early surveillance criterion', so the dashboard would pass when that chip is ticked. Web, 2026-09-25 (fix-web-screening): now observed in the harness — the preventive-screening engine reads the "Family history: …" and "Lynch syndrome" comorbidity entries, which the dashboard passes too; web removed from unverified.
CRC < 50 in a sister plus endometrial cancer in the mother: Lynch syndrome must be considered — tumour MMR/MSI testing of the affected relative and genetics referral.

guideline.name: US Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer — screening recommendations
guideline.section: Family history: FDR with CRC or advanced adenoma < 60 years, or two FDRs at any age — colonoscopy every 5 years beginning at 40 or 10 years before the youngest affected relative
guideline.citation: Rex DK, Boland CR, Dominitz JA, et al. Colorectal cancer screening: recommendations for physicians and patients from the U.S. Multi-Society Task Force on Colorectal Cancer. Gastroenterology. 2017;153:307–323.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guidelines — colorectal cancer screening
guideline.section: Average risk: start at 45; one first-degree relative with CRC or advanced adenoma diagnosed < 60, or two FDRs at any age: colonoscopy from 40 (or 10 years before the youngest affected relative) every 5 years
guideline.citation: Shaukat A, Kahi CJ, Burke CA, et al. ACG clinical guidelines: colorectal cancer screening 2021. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116:458–479.

guideline.name: BSG/ACPGBI/UKCGG guidelines — management of hereditary colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Family-history assessment; Lynch syndrome suspected with CRC < 50 or Lynch-spectrum cancers (e.g. endometrial) in relatives — tumour MMR/MSI testing of the affected relative and clinical genetics referral
guideline.citation: Monahan KJ, Bradshaw N, Dolwani S, et al. Guidelines for the management of hereditary colorectal cancer from the British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG)/Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland (ACPGBI)/United Kingdom Cancer Genetics Group (UKCGG). Gut. 2020;69:411–444.

guideline.name: NICE DG27 — molecular testing strategies for Lynch syndrome in people with colorectal cancer
guideline.section: Offer MMR immunohistochemistry or MSI testing to everyone with colorectal cancer when first diagnosed, to identify Lynch syndrome
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Molecular testing strategies for Lynch syndrome in people with colorectal cancer. Diagnostics guidance DG27, 2017.

rationale: An FDR with colorectal cancer before 50 and an endometrial cancer in another FDR raise the family to increased risk with Lynch features. US guidance: colonoscopy from 40, 5-yearly; UK guidance: seek the relative's tumour MMR status and refer to genetics.
